answer.likely_cause: Both east-side chargers (C2 faulted, C4 on planned maintenance) are unavailable, leaving all 7 G3 robots unable to charge; 5 are queued at CHG-EAST and 2 are blocked in the corridor behind them, starving PS3 of totes.
answer.reasoning: C4 went offline for firmware maintenance at 12:30 (E9). C2 raised a CHG-214 contactor fault at 14:02 (E12). G3 robots have affinity only to C2 and C4 (E14, E31), so when both failed they queued rather than failing over. Five robots (R15, R16, R18, R19, R21) are stuck in QUEUED_CHARGE with ~14% battery (E1, E2, E4, E5, E7), and R17/R20 are BLOCKED in CHG-CORR-E behind the queue (E3, E6), matching the WCS-430 'no available robot in G3' alerts that began at 14:11 (E22).

evidence.why: C4 taken out of service at 12:30 for firmware upgrade until 17:30 — one of the two east chargers already gone before the incident
C2 raised CHG-214 contactor fault at 14:02, removing the last available east charger
Fleet log confirms R15 arrived CHG-EAST and found both C2 FAULT and C4 MAINTENANCE — no charger available
R15 has been QUEUED_CHARGE since 14:03 at 13.7% — below the 15% charge threshold, unable to work
R17 BLOCKED in CHG-CORR-E with AMR-207 since 14:10 — corridor gridlocked behind queued robots
R20 also BLOCKED in CHG-CORR-E with AMR-207 since 14:11 — second robot trapped behind R17
WCS-430 repeated 5 times 14:11–14:19: no available robot in G3, 12 tasks pending for PS3 — confirms station starvation
PS3 tote throughput declining from 14:00 onward, 5 min idle already by 14:00 interval — timeline matches charger failures

ruled_out.what: INC-0137 / PS3 scanner offline (PS-601)
ruled_out.why: Robots are not arriving at PS3 at all (E22 shows no robot available in G3); in INC-0137 robots were present but the scanner was offline. No PS-601 fault in evidence.

ruled_out.what: Aisle blockage as root cause (INC-0130 pattern, AMR-207 primary)
ruled_out.why: AMR-207 on R17/R20 is a secondary effect — they are blocked in the charging corridor by the queue of QUEUED_CHARGE robots, not by a debris or e-stop fault in a pick aisle. No AMR-305/310 fault present.

ruled_out.what: WCS-402 task rejects causing PS3 starvation
ruled_out.why: E18 shows a single WCS-402 reject at 14:05 for PS5, not PS3, and it is isolated. The PS3 starvation is explained entirely by no available G3 robots (E22); WCS-402 is unrelated noise.

similar_incident.why: Identical pattern: C4 out of service + C2 CHG-214 fault → all G3 robots queued in CHG-EAST → PS3 starved. Same fault codes (CHG-214, AMR-207, WCS-430). Fix was to reroute G3 affinity to C1/C3 and power-cycle C2.

runbook.next_step: In the fleet manager, change G3 charger affinity from C2/C4 to C1/C3 (west) so queued robots can charge immediately — prioritise R15, R18, R19 at ~13–14% battery. Then power-cycle C2 at its isolator to attempt CHG-214 clearance.

check_next: Confirm C2 charger status after power-cycle — if CHG-214 returns within an hour, isolate C2 and raise a maintenance request for contactor replacement (as per RB-01 step 4).
Verify R17 and R20 in CHG-CORR-E clear automatically once the queued robots ahead of them begin moving to west chargers.
Once G3 robots start charging on C1/C3, confirm WCS-430 alerts stop and PS3 tote arrivals resume before restoring normal affinity.
answer.prevention: Schedule C2 and C4 maintenance on separate days so both east chargers are never simultaneously unavailable; a simple fleet-manager alert when both chargers on one side are FAULT/MAINTENANCE simultaneously would catch this before robots deplete.

answer.likely_cause: R07 triggered an emergency stop in aisle A04 due to a safety field obstruction (AMR-305), blocking R03 and R05 behind it and slowing PS1 tote delivery.
answer.reasoning: R07 entered FAULT with AMR-305 at 09:41 in zone A04 (E7, E9), indicating its lidar detected an obstruction and triggered an e-stop. R03 then became BLOCKED at 09:43 with AMR-207 citing R07 as the obstacle (E10), and R05 followed at 09:46 citing R03 (E11). Three G1 robots serving PS1 are now stuck in A04, reducing tote flow to PS1 (E12). PS1 throughput has been gradually declining but the last tote was still delivered at 09:44 (E12); the station will idle soon if the blockage is not cleared.

evidence.why: R07 in FAULT state, zone A04, fault AMR-305 since 09:41 — the first robot in the chain
Fleet log confirms R07 AMR-305 safety field obstruction emergency stop at 09:41:07 in aisle A04
R03 BLOCKED in A04 since 09:43, AMR-207, battery 22.8% — queued behind R07, low battery adds urgency
R05 BLOCKED in A04 since 09:46, AMR-207 — queued behind R03
Log confirms R03 path blocked by R07 at 09:43
Log confirms R05 path blocked by R03 at 09:46
PS1 throughput declining (352→340 picks/h) and last tote at 09:44 — station will idle without intervention
AMR-305 = safety field obstruction CRITICAL; AMR-207 = path blocked WARNING — confirms chain pattern

ruled_out.what: Charger failure starving PS1 of robots (similar to INC-0142)
ruled_out.why: No CHG fault codes present; R03 battery is low (22.8%) but R05 is at 84.6% and R07 at 60.6%. The blockage in A04 explains the slowdown without any charger issue (E8 shows 33 other robots normal).

ruled_out.what: Conveyor jam at PS1 outbound (similar to INC-0125)
ruled_out.why: No CNV fault codes reported; PS1 station data shows totes were still arriving at 09:44 and the operator is logged in. The slowdown is robot-supply-side, not conveyor-side.

ruled_out.what: PS1 operator or scanner issue
ruled_out.why: Operator is logged in and picks/h have been consistent across all 15-min intervals; other stations are at similar rates (E13), ruling out a station-local fault.

similar_incident.why: Identical pattern: AMR-305 e-stop on one robot in an aisle, two AMR-207 blocked robots queued behind it. INC-0128 root cause was debris (shrink-wrap) in the lidar field — the same cause should be checked here first.

runbook.next_step: Put aisle A04 into maintenance mode in the fleet manager immediately, then walk to R07 (the FAULT robot) wearing hi-vis and aisle lock-out tag to look for debris, a fallen tote or any obstruction in its safety field.

check_next: Inspect the floor around R07 in A04 for debris (shrink-wrap, strapping, labels) or a fallen tote that triggered the safety field.
After clearing the obstruction and resetting R07's e-stop, confirm R03 battery (22.8%) — it may need to route to a charger before resuming delivery rather than continuing its task.
If R07 faults again in A04 within 24 hours, take it out of service per RB-02 step 6 and raise a maintenance inspection.
answer.prevention: Add a scheduled aisle debris sweep at shift start and after peak replenishment periods; a simple alert triggering when any AMR-305 persists for more than 5 minutes in the same zone would flag this before a queue forms.

answer.likely_cause: WMS slotting batch SLT-8841 re-coded 212 locations in the L-07 range at 16:15 before the WCS location master was synchronised, causing WCS to reject all tasks referencing those locations and starving PS4 and PS6 of work.
answer.reasoning: Slotting batch SLT-8841 applied at 16:15 (E16) immediately preceded the first WCS-402 rejects at 16:18 (E17, E18), all targeting L-07 locations. Station throughput at PS4 and PS6 dropped sharply in the 16:15 interval (E19, E20) while all other stations remained normal (E21), confirming the problem is task-supply not robot capacity. This is the same WMS-ahead-of-WCS-sync failure seen in INC-0131 and INC-0139.

evidence.why: Slotting batch SLT-8841 re-coded 212 L-07 locations at 16:15, the trigger event
12 WCS-402 rejects for PS6 from 16:18, all citing unknown L-07 locations
12 WCS-402 rejects for PS4 from 16:20, same pattern
PS4 throughput halved in the 16:15 interval (344→196 picks/h, 5 min idle), matching reject onset
PS6 throughput halved in the 16:15 interval (336→188 picks/h, 5 min idle), matching reject onset
All other stations normal at 16:15, ruling out a fleet-wide or systemic issue
Confirms WCS-402 = task rejected due to unknown storage location
RB-03 step 2 directly covers WCS-402 after a slotting update: trigger WCS location master resync then ask WMS to resend rejected tasks

ruled_out.what: INC-0144 look-alike: low picks/h caused by wave composition (bulky orders)
ruled_out.why: INC-0144 had no fault codes and affected only PS6. Here WCS-402 errors are present for both PS4 and PS6, and the drop is tied to the slotting event, not order mix (E17, E18, E21).

ruled_out.what: Robot battery / capacity shortage causing work starvation
ruled_out.why: R35 and R36 raised low-battery charge requests (E14, E15) but this is normal fleet behaviour and predates the throughput drop. All other stations served by different groups are unaffected (E21), and 28 other robots are working normally (E13).

ruled_out.what: Other WCS reject codes (WCS-401 invalid SKU, WCS-410 schema, WCS-420 duplicate)
ruled_out.why: All logged errors are exclusively WCS-402 (E17, E18, E22), and the timing matches a slotting update, not a system upgrade or failover.

similar_incident.why: Identical root cause: WMS slotting update re-coded L-07 locations before WCS master data sync, producing a burst of WCS-402 rejects that starved PS4 and PS6. Fixed by WCS location master resync and WMS task resend (RB-03).

runbook.next_step: In the WCS interface monitor, filter rejects for the last 30 minutes, confirm all are WCS-402 for L-07 locations, then trigger the WCS location master resync and ask WMS support to resend the rejected tasks (T-513014, T-513005 and all others in the queue).

check_next: Confirm all WCS-402 rejects reference L-07 locations (matching SLT-8841 range) and that no other location ranges are affected.
After triggering WCS location master resync, verify the WCS-402 reject rate drops to zero before asking WMS to resend tasks.
Check whether the WCS location master resync completed successfully and PS4/PS6 throughput recovers toward pre-incident levels (~340 picks/h).
answer.prevention: Implement an automated pre-check that blocks WMS task release for any location codes not yet present in the WCS master, and add an alert that fires when the WCS-402 rate exceeds a threshold within 5 minutes of a slotting batch apply — a simple rule-based alert would cover this recurring failure mode (recommended in INC-0131, INC-0139, and RB-03).

answer.likely_cause: R31 ran its battery down to critical (10%) because its charge request was lost during the scheduled fleet manager restart at 05:41, mirroring INC-0130.
answer.reasoning: R31 hit fault AMR-112 (battery critical stop) at 06:39 with exactly 10% battery (E1, E6, E14). A scheduled fleet manager restart occurred at 05:41 with a 90-second heartbeat timeout affecting all 40 robots including R31 (E3, E4, E5). Per INC-0130, the same fault pattern (AMR-112, ~10% battery, fleet manager restart) was caused by a charge request sent during the restart window being silently dropped, leaving the robot to run down without ever reaching a charger. No other robots are faulted (E2), ruling out a systemic issue.

evidence.why: R31 in FAULT state, zone TR-2, battery 10%, fault code AMR-112 since 06:39
Fleet log confirms AMR-112 battery critical stop for R31 at 06:39:09
AMR-112 = Battery critical - robot stopped; confirms this is a battery exhaustion stop, not a safety or comms fault
Scheduled fleet manager restart at 05:41 created a window where charge requests could be lost
All 40 robots lost heartbeat for ~90 s during restart; any charge request queued in this window would not have been processed
Fleet manager came back online at 05:43:51; requests sent during the gap were not replayed
R31 already placed in manual mode by eng_early at 06:41 — robot is safe to tow
INC-0130 is an exact match: AMR-112, ~10% battery, charge request lost during fleet manager restart; resolved in 30 min via RB-04

ruled_out.what: INC-0128 / debris or safety-field obstruction (AMR-305/AMR-207)
ruled_out.why: R31's fault code is AMR-112 (battery critical), not AMR-305 or AMR-207; no debris or e-stop evidence present (E1, E14)

ruled_out.what: INC-0132 / Wi-Fi access point failure (AMR-401/AMR-410)
ruled_out.why: Only R31 is faulted; 39 other robots are working normally, ruling out a network zone outage (E2). R31's fault is AMR-112, not AMR-410

ruled_out.what: Battery hardware degradation (fast drain unrelated to missed charge)
ruled_out.why: Only one robot is affected and the fleet manager restart provides a clear mechanism for a missed charge request; battery health report can be checked later per RB-04 step 5 (E18)

similar_incident.why: Identical fault code (AMR-112), near-identical battery level (~9-10%), and a fleet manager restart immediately before the robot should have requested charging — same root cause, same fix path

runbook.next_step: Confirm R31 is already in manual mode (E7 shows it is), then tow it to the nearest free charger using the tow handle; verify the charge request is queued once docked.

check_next: Check fleet logs between 05:41 and 05:44 for an AMR-101 charge request from R31 — absence confirms the request was dropped during the restart window.
Once R31 is on charge, pull its battery health report to confirm drain rate was normal and no hardware fault contributed.
Review whether the FM-3.8.2 patch replay mechanism re-queues pending charge requests after restart; if not, raise a software change request.
answer.prevention: Configure a fleet-manager post-restart reconciliation check that re-evaluates battery levels for all robots and re-queues any missing charge requests; a simple alert firing when any robot is below 12% and not en-route to or on a charger would also catch this before it becomes a critical stop.

answer.likely_cause: Recurring tote jam at merge M2 caused by misaligned or loose photo-eye PE-M2-03 bracket blocking the outbound conveyor from PS5.
answer.reasoning: PE-M2-03 has blocked three times in under 90 minutes (E9, E12, E15), each time causing the PS5 outbound spur to fill and pause the station (E10, E13, E16). The same fault pattern (CNV-501 then CNV-520) has occurred in three prior incidents (INC-0125, INC-0134, INC-0143), all traced to the same loose bracket on PE-M2-03. Operator resets at M2 (E11, E14) gave only temporary relief, confirming the bracket has not been permanently fixed and MR-2207 remains open.

evidence.why: First PE-M2-03 block at 11:12, triggering the jam chain
PS5 outbound spur full 60 s later, station paused
PE-M2-03 blocks again at 11:24 after operator reset — jam recurred
Third block at 11:31, confirming persistent fault at M2
PS5 paused again at 11:32, directly linked to E15
PS5 throughput collapsed from 368 picks/h to 0 then 140 picks/h with repeated 'outbound spur full' notes
INC-0143 (Oct 2026) confirmed MR-2207 still open — bracket replacement never completed
RB-05 step 3 explicitly calls out PE-M2-03 bracket as known repeat offender at Merge M2

ruled_out.what: Robot group G5 shortage causing tote starvation
ruled_out.why: Symptom is totes cannot leave PS5, not totes failing to arrive. R28–R34 show normal states (E1–E7) and 33 other robots are healthy (E8).

ruled_out.what: PS6 outage causing network-wide conveyor backup
ruled_out.why: PS6 shows 0 picks/h (E18) but all other stations are running normally and the fault codes are isolated to M2/PS5 spur, not a shared trunk.

ruled_out.what: One-off tote jam unrelated to bracket (as in a first-time incident)
ruled_out.why: Three prior tickets (INC-0125, INC-0134, INC-0143) with identical fault codes all traced to the same loose PE-M2-03 bracket; MR-2207 is still open, so the root hardware defect was never resolved.

similar_incident.why: Identical fault codes CNV-501 + CNV-520, same merge M2 / PE-M2-03 bracket root cause, and MR-2207 explicitly noted as still open — making this a direct continuation of that recurring fault.

runbook.next_step: Stop and lock out the M2 conveyor section at its local panel, then clear any jammed totes and inspect PE-M2-03 bracket alignment before restarting.

check_next: Walk merge M2 and confirm totes are jammed at PE-M2-03; check whether the bracket is visibly loose or beam is angled down onto the belt.
After clearing, watch three totes pass PE-M2-03 cleanly before releasing the PS5 station pause.
Check MR-2207 status — if still open, escalate immediately for same-day bracket replacement; this is the fourth jam in under 90 days.
answer.prevention: MR-2207 bracket replacement must be completed urgently; a simple alert rule triggering a P1 maintenance ticket if CNV-501 fires more than once in any 90-day window on the same photo-eye would have caught this earlier.

answer.likely_cause: WCS task allocator (release 5.8.2, reloaded at 19:30) is repeatedly assigning tasks to already-busy G6 robots, causing 90-second re-queue delays that starve PS6 of totes.
answer.reasoning: From 20:08 onward, four different G6 robots (R36, R38, R35, R40) each rejected a WCS task because they were still executing a prior one, triggering a 90-second re-queue each time (E11–E15). This pattern started ~38 minutes before the incident report and aligns exactly with the WCS config reload at 19:30 (E10). PS6 throughput fell steadily from 356 picks/h at 19:45 to 196 picks/h at 20:30 (E17), and average task wait time hit 3m40s vs a normal <30s (E16). No charger fault or robot hardware fault is evident for G6.

evidence.why: WCS task allocator reloaded with release 5.8.2 at 19:30, just before degradation began — likely introduced a scheduling defect
R36 rejected a task at 20:08 because it was still executing a prior task; 90-second re-queue penalty applied
R38 rejected a task at 20:17 for the same reason — pattern repeating across multiple robots
R35 rejected a task at 20:26 — now three of six G6 robots affected
R36 rejected again at 20:33 — recurring, not a one-off
R40 rejected a task at 20:44 — four distinct G6 robots hit, confirming systemic allocator issue
PS6 average task wait 3m40s over last 30 min vs normal <30s — confirms robots not being assigned promptly
PS6 throughput declining steadily since 20:00, idle time growing — consistent with intermittent robot availability caused by re-queue delays

ruled_out.what: Charger unavailability starving G6 robots (similar to INC-0142)
ruled_out.why: C4 was in planned maintenance (E9) but was back in service by 17:30. No G6 robot is in QUEUED_CHARGE; all six G6 robots show active working states with batteries well above the 15% charge-seek threshold (E2–E7). R37 at 20.9% is the lowest but still DELIVERING, not queuing.

ruled_out.what: INC-0144 wave composition issue
ruled_out.why: In INC-0144 robots were working normally and throughput was low due to bulky orders. Here robots are actively rejecting tasks due to an allocator conflict — a different mechanism — and all other stations are performing normally (E18), ruling out a wave-wide composition problem.

ruled_out.what: Conveyor jam at PS6 (similar to INC-0125)
ruled_out.why: INC-0125 involved fault codes CNV-501/CNV-520 and a full outbound lane. No conveyor fault codes are present here, and the symptom is totes arriving in bursts with gaps, not a blocked outbound lane.

similar_incident.why: No prior ticket matches a WCS allocator regression causing task-rejection loops. INC-0142 is superficially similar (station starved) but root cause was a charger fault, not a scheduler defect.

runbook.next_step: Contact the WCS/controls team immediately: ask them to review the task allocator logic in release 5.8.2 for a bug that assigns a new task to a robot before its current task completes, and consider rolling back to the previous release or reloading the prior config while the fix is investigated.

check_next: Confirm the task-rejection warnings (E11–E15) started after 19:30 and were absent before the config reload — check WCS logs from 18:30–19:30 for any prior rejections on G6 robots.
Check whether other station groups (G1–G5) have similar task-rejection warnings since 19:30 — if yes, the allocator bug is site-wide; if no, it may be G6-specific config.
Ask the WCS team for the diff between release 5.8.2 and the previous version, specifically in the task-assignment readiness check logic.
answer.prevention: Add a real-time alert that fires when any robot group generates more than 2 task-rejection 'still executing' warnings within 10 minutes, and enforce a staging/canary rollout policy for WCS allocator releases during live operations.

answer.likely_cause: A software or data mismatch is serving incorrect product images to the PS2 display — possibly a stale cache, a failed content sync, or a WCS/UI configuration error on the PS2 terminal.
answer.reasoning: The symptom is wrong product images on the PS2 screen, which points to a display/data layer problem rather than a hardware or robot issue. PS2 throughput and robot delivery are normal (E15, E3, E4, E6), so the physical pick flow is unaffected. No fault codes, UI errors, or content-sync logs are present in the evidence to confirm a specific cause.

evidence.why: PS2 throughput is normal (26–31 totes per 15 min, zero idle time) — robots and totes are arriving correctly, so the issue is isolated to the display layer
R10 is actively delivering to PS2-IN, confirming tote supply is working
R11 also delivering to PS2-IN, further confirming normal robot operations at PS2
R13 is AT_STATION at PS2, consistent with normal station activity
33 other robots reporting normal states — no fleet-wide issue that could explain a display fault
Other stations running at comparable pick rates — problem is specific to PS2, not a site-wide WCS outage

ruled_out.what: Robot/tote starvation at PS2 (similar to INC-0137 scanner offline)
ruled_out.why: PS2 picks/h and tote counts are healthy with zero idle time (E15); operators are picking, just double-checking images

ruled_out.what: Charger C4 maintenance causing fleet disruption at PS2
ruled_out.why: C4 serves groups G3/G4 (east affinity per RB-01); PS2 is served by G2 which uses C1/C3 (west) — charger maintenance is unrelated. PS2 robot telemetry is also normal (E3, E4, E6)

ruled_out.what: WCS task-queue delays (E10–E14) affecting PS2
ruled_out.why: Those warnings involve R35, R36, R38, R40 and affect PS6 wait times (E14), not PS2. PS2 throughput shows no degradation (E15)

similar_incident.why: No past ticket in the evidence covers wrong product images on a pick station display.

runbook.next_step: Log into the PS2 terminal and check which product image is displayed versus the tote/SKU currently at the station; then check the WCS product-image service or UI config for PS2 to see if a sync or cache refresh is needed.

check_next: Compare the SKU shown on the PS2 screen against the WCS task record for the tote currently at the station — confirm whether the mismatch is in the image asset, the SKU mapping, or the task assignment
Check the PS2 terminal application logs for any content-sync errors, failed image downloads, or UI configuration load failures around 22:00–22:10
Restart or refresh the PS2 display application (after confirming with the operator) and verify whether images correct themselves — if yes, a stale cache or failed sync is the cause
answer.prevention: Add a monitoring alert that compares the SKU in the active WCS task against the product ID embedded in the displayed image asset on each pick station screen, triggering a warning on any mismatch; a simple rule-based check would suffice.
